sections.h2: Which Scott County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Scott County Property and Taxation Services handles both sides of the bill: the assessors who set value and the staff who collect payment. It sits in the Government Center in Shakopee, the county seat, and answers questions at 952-496-8115 or propertytax@co.scott.mn.us.

The department employs eleven licensed assessors who estimate market value and classification for roughly 58,000 parcels. They also hold the public meetings where owners can discuss a value. Cities and townships in the county, including Prior Lake, Savage, Jordan and Belle Plaine, each add their own levy to the single statement a parcel receives, and so do the school districts and special districts that overlap them.

The county's assessment page also explains the switch from the old homestead market value credit to the homestead market value exclusion, which changes how a homestead house is valued for tax and is worth reading before you compare two years of statements.

sections.h2: When are Scott County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half of the year's tax is due in mid-May and the second half in mid-October. The county's payment page gave Thursday, October 15, 2026 as the second-half date, so that deadline has passed, and the next one is the first half of 2027.

Under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01, a half left unpaid on its due date picks up 2 percent on homestead property or 4 percent on nonhomestead property. The same increase repeats on the first day of the following month. Each later month through December adds 1 percent, with ceilings of 8 percent on homesteads and 12 percent on other property. A treasurer must also waive the penalty once when the envelope was postmarked within one business day after the due date.

That waiver matters more now that the Postal Service dates mail when it first processes it. Scott County recommends that mailers carry the payment to a post office counter and ask for a manual postmark, mail several business days early, or pay electronically.

sections.h2: What is the best way to pay a Scott County tax bill?
sections.html:
Paying online is the quickest, and it avoids a trip to Shakopee on a busy deadline. The county's online payment center accepts e-check, debit and credit cards, and it does not work with the Internet Explorer browser.

  • If you wait for a receipt at the Government Center on the due date, staff add your name to a standby list, so the county suggests using another route.
  • Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to be on time.
  • Property under a confession of judgment contract needs its delinquent amounts checked with taxation staff at 952-496-8115 before you pay.
  • Owners can subscribe to e-notices through the same online payment center and get statements by email.

Whichever route you choose, keep the confirmation for your records.

sections.h2: What does Scott County look like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Scott County covers 368 square miles in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro area, which makes it the third smallest Minnesota county by land area. The Minnesota River forms its northern and western edge. Eight cities share the county: Belle Plaine, Credit River, Elko New Market, Jordan, New Prague (partly in Le Sueur County), Prior Lake, Savage and Shakopee.

The county was organized on March 5, 1853 and takes its name from General Winfield Scott. Farming, lumbering and fur trading along the river shaped the early economy. Suburban growth then pushed the population from 89,498 in 2000 to 150,928 in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 159,017. The Shakopee-Mdewakanton Indian Reservation lies entirely inside the county, within Prior Lake and Shakopee, and Canterbury Park, Valleyfair, Mystic Lake and the Renaissance Festival draw visitors to the county.

The Census Bureau's latest housing figures show a county of owners:

  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.8 percent, with 54,971 households averaging 2.78 people.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $419,400.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,329. Median gross rent: $1,568.
  • Median household income: $119,314. Mean commute to work: 24.8 minutes.
  • Housing units on July 1, 2025: 59,179, and 883 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Scott County valuation?
sections.html:
First collect proof that the assessor's value is off, such as a recent appraisal or a recent sale of a similar home. Then contact the assessor for your city or township and, if useful, visit the office.

If you still disagree, attend the Open Book meeting or the Local Board of Appeal and Equalization meeting listed on your value notice. From either of those you may go on to the County Board of Appeal and Equalization. The final step is a petition to the Minnesota Tax Court, which can be filed after you receive the value notice and before April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

Scott County accepts service of tax petitions by email or through a drop box outside the Government Center, and it will not acknowledge anything delivered after 4:30 p.m. on the filing deadline. The county reminds petitioners that they must still file with the district court administrator, and an emailed acknowledgement can serve as proof of service. If no reply arrives within 24 hours, follow up.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a Scott County house sells?
sections.html:
The tax stays attached to the parcel, so a seller who owes delinquent years should have the figure confirmed with taxation staff before closing. The buyer's deed has its own state costs. Minnesota Statutes section 287.21 sets the deed tax at 0.33 percent of net consideration on sales above $3,000, and $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less.

When the deed is recorded, a certificate of value goes to the county auditor under section 272.115. That filing is a condition of homestead treatment, and the assessor removes the homestead classification for the next assessment year from a sold property unless the buyer applies and qualifies. As a seller, ask your closing agent how the half-year already paid is handled in the settlement figures.

Anyone selling a Scott County house with tax owing, an inherited property, or a place that needs repairs can request a cash offer and ask the buyer to work from the payoff amount the county gives you. Having the statement and parcel number ready speeds that conversation up.

faqs.q: What is the Scott County property tax phone number?
faqs.a: Call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115, or email propertytax@co.scott.mn.us.

faqs.q: When was the 2026 second half of Scott County tax due?
faqs.a: The county's payment page lists Thursday, October 15, 2026 as the second-half due date, and it has passed, so any unpaid balance is accruing penalty.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Scott County tax online?
faqs.a: An e-check costs $1.50 per transaction, and a debit or credit card costs 2.3 percent of the payment. The county lists fees only for the online route.

faqs.q: Where is the Scott County drop box for property tax?
faqs.a: The outdoor box is in the circular driveway off Atwood Street between 4th and 5th Avenue in Shakopee, next to the USPS mailbox. County libraries also hold a drop box in the weeks before each deadline.

faqs.q: What is the last step if I still disagree with my value?
faqs.a: File a petition with the Minnesota Tax Court after you get the value notice and before April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Serve a copy on Scott County and file it with the district court administrator.
